chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, who said: Musa ibn Umar al-Baghdadi narrated to us, from Ibn Sinan, from Awn ibn Ma'in the seller of hats, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) say:
Whoever meets people with one face and disparages them with another face, will come on the Day of Resurrection with two tongues of fire.

key_terms.عابهم: Disparaged/reproached them; from the root عيب meaning to find fault or defect in someone
key_terms.لسانان من نار: Two tongues of fire; the eschatological punishment matching the sin of speaking differently to and about people
key_terms.وجه: Face; here used metaphorically to denote outward behavior or demeanor toward others
key_terms.يوم القيامة: Day of Resurrection; the Day of Judgment when all deeds are accounted for

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for being two-faced in Islam according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) warns against two-facedness and hypocrisy in social dealings. This teaching, delivered in the context of the scholarly circles of Kufa and Qum in the 2nd century AH where backbiting was a widespread social vice, emphasizes that presenting a pleasant facade to people while secretly maligning them is a grave sin. The punishment of "two tongues of fire" on the Day of Resurrection serves as a vivid eschatological deterrent, symbolically connecting the instrument of the sin (the duplicitous tongue) to the form of the punishment.
